To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a novel hybrid method of facial feature extraction and facial emotion recognition that uses Viola-Jones object detectors and Harris Corner Key-Points to extract faces from images, and uses principal component and linear discriminant analysis and histogram-of-oriented-gradiant feature extraction to train a multi class predictor that uses support vector machine classifiers for classification of seven fundamental human facial emotions.

we developed a novel approach for detecting human facial expressions that uses Viola-Jones object detectors and Harris corners to locate faces and facial features, and uses principal component and linear discriminant analysis to calculate a basis that emphasizes the separation between emotions.

we were able to achieve an accuracy of 81% in the classification of seven facial expressions using a hybrid approach that combines a fast eigenvector projection step with a slower, but more accurate, HOG feature extraction and SVM classification step.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automatic recognition of human emotions in images and videos using facial features as an indication of the emotion.
facial feature recognition for emotion detection.
the automatic recognition of human emotions from facial expressions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method can be used to classify human emotion in images with a reasonable accuracy, but it is not as accurate or fast as other existing methods.
the proposed hybrid method for facial emotion classification performs well and is a good compromise between accuracy and run-time.
this hybrid approach is a reasonable alternative to the HOG approach, and is more accurate than the Viola-Jones approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hybrid approach is a good compromise for speed and accuracy, and that the Viola-Jones detector is a good choice for face detection and the HOG approach is a good choice when facial features need to be extracted.

our hybrid feature extraction method, using a combination of Viola-Jones object detection and Harris corner key-point extraction, allows for the quick extraction of faces from images and a reasonable classification of the seven fundamental human emotions.
our hybrid approach is faster and more accurate than using the HOD approach exclusively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of the Viola-Jones detector and HOG feature extraction can be used to achieve a reasonable level of accuracy for facial expression recognition.
we have created a fast, accurate, and computationally efficient algorithm that is capable of recognizing seven human facial expressions.
we can use a hybrid approach to extract features and predict emotions in images with high accuracy and in a reasonable amount of time.
